stays around Mandeh and the bay

children.text: West Sumatra gets visited in one direction. Travellers land at Padang, drive north to Bukittinggi and the Harau Valley, and never look the other way. The bay at Carocok Tarusan, which everybody calls Mandeh, sits about ninety minutes south of the airport, and almost nobody builds a trip around it.

This route does. Seven days, one airport, two bases and a lot of time in small wooden boats. It comes with an honest catch that most tour listings still hide: Cubadak, the island that gave the bay its reputation, lost its only resort in 2021 and has never replaced it. Plan around that and this coast is one of the better weeks in Sumatra. Plan for the brochure version and you will spend the trip looking for something that closed five years ago.
Who this trip is for

This suits couples, friends and solo travellers who are happy on the water, comfortable eating whatever the warung has cooked that day, and not looking for anything organised. It works best as a second Indonesia trip, or as the coastal half of a Sumatra trip that would otherwise be all jungle and volcanoes.

It is not for you if you want dive centres, beach clubs or a spa. There is no dive industry here in the Pulau Weh sense, no nightlife, and once you leave Padang very little English. Families can do it, but the good days are boat days with limited shade, so it is easier with older children than with toddlers.
Is Mandeh Bay worth visiting?

Yes, if what you want is a quiet coast rather than a resort. Mandeh Bay is a sheltered bay south of Padang, ringed by small islands, mangrove channels and steep green headlands, about ninety minutes away by road. It is genuinely good looking and genuinely undeveloped, and those two facts are the same fact.

Local tourism copy sells it as the Raja Ampat of West Sumatra, and that oversells it. The water is warm and clear enough for easy snorkelling, the coral is patchy, and the fish life is ordinary by Indonesian standards. What is unusual is the setting: according to Indonesia's official tourism site the bay is fringed by roughly 389 hectares of mangrove forest, and you can spend an afternoon paddling through it without seeing another boat.
The other reason to come is that the province around it is excellent. Padang has the best food in Sumatra and one of the easiest airports to reach it by, and the
highlands around Bukittinggi and the Harau Valley
are two hours the other way if you want to bolt them on.
Trip at a glance
Duration:
7 days, 6 nights.
Route:
Padang for two nights, a day out to the Bungus islands, then three nights on the Mandeh side of the bay, a night near Painan or back in Padang, and out from Padang.
Pace:
Relaxed. Two road transfers of ninety minutes or so, three boat days, and enough slack to lose a day to weather without breaking the trip.
Best season:

Roughly May to September is the drier stretch on this coast, with July often the driest month and November the wettest. Sumatra is wet year round, so read that as odds rather than a guarantee, and check a recent forecast before you commit to boat days.
Getting in:

Fly to Minangkabau International Airport, code PDG, which sits about 23 kilometres north of Padang. Domestic connections come mostly through Jakarta; fare aggregators were listing around 49 departures a day on that route in September 2026, the quickest under two hours, with fares starting in the region of 550,000 rupiah.
Compare Jakarta to Padang flights and buses
before you fix the dates, because the cheap seats move around.
Budget:
This is a cheap week by Indonesian standards, apart from the boats. Our
Indonesia travel costs guide
puts mid-range travel at 70 to 100 US dollars a day per person, and on this coast you will sit at the low end unless you charter boats privately.
Why this route makes sense

The bay is small, and that is the planning problem. A boat can cover the headline islands in one long day, which is exactly why most people come as a day trip from Padang, look at it for four hours and leave. The trip is much better at three nights, because the good parts are the early mornings, the mangroves and the villages, and none of those survive a day trip.

So the shape is: warm up on the water near Padang, where boats are cheap and the logistics are forgiving, then move south and stay. Putting the Bungus day first also means that if the sea is rough on your first attempt you lose a warm-up day rather than the day you came for.

Finishing back through Painan rather than driving straight to the airport gives you a buffer. This is a coast where a boat can be cancelled at short notice, and you do not want your only flexible day to be the one before your flight.
Where should you stay around Mandeh Bay?

Split the week between Padang and the bay itself. Padang has hotels at every price and the food you came for, but it is ninety minutes from the boats, so it does not work as a Mandeh base. On the bay you are choosing between simple homestays and cottages around Mandeh village and Sungai Nyalo, or more conventional hotels thirty minutes further south in Painan.

cells: Padang city
Hotels at every price, the airport train, and the best eating of the trip
Ninety minutes from the bay, so it works as bookends, not as a base
Mandeh village and Sungai Nyalo
Closest to the boats, small cottages and homestays on the water
Basic rooms, almost no dinner choice, and you depend on your host for boats
Painan and Carocok Painan
The nearest real town, more hotels, shops and a beach of its own
Thirty minutes further south, with the bay views behind you
Pulau Cubadak
Still the best looking water in the bay
Its only resort closed in 2021, so this is a day visit, not a stay

children.text: In practice, book
rooms in Padang
for the city nights, then compare
stays around Mandeh and the bay
and
hotels in Painan
for the middle of the week. Inventory on the bay side is thin and much of it is not online at all, so if the listings look empty, that is the market, not a mistake.
What happened to the resort on Pulau Cubadak?

Cubadak Paradiso Village, the Italian run resort that opened on the island in 1992 and put Mandeh on the map for foreign travellers, closed permanently on 31 August 2021 after eighteen months without guests. Nothing has replaced it. Older blog posts, tour listings and hotel aggregators still show it, which is the single most common way people get this trip wrong.

Practically, this means Cubadak is a stop on a boat loop and a snorkel, not a place you sleep. It also means the bay lost the one operation that ran reliable, English speaking boat trips, so most of what you book now is arranged locally, by phone or through your homestay.
How much does a Mandeh Bay boat trip cost?

Boats are chartered by the boat, not by the seat, and one boat takes about twelve people. The official tariff sheet published for the Mandeh tourist area lists a short island loop at around 750,000 rupiah and the fuller loop, adding Kapo-Kapo and the Sungai Nyalo mangroves, at around 850,000. Treat those as the floor.

cells: Pulau Setan only
A short hop to the nearest island and back
Around Rp 75,000 per person
Short island loop
Sironjong Gadang, Sironjong Ketek, past Cubadak, Pulau Setan, Sungai Gemuruh
Around Rp 750,000 per boat, up to about 12 people
Full bay loop
The short loop plus Kapo-Kapo village and the Sungai Nyalo mangroves
Around Rp 850,000 per boat, up to about 12 people
Outer islands run
Pulau Pagang, Pamutusan and Teluk Sikulo, further offshore
Around Rp 1,500,000 per boat, plus a small per-person entry

children.text: Two honest caveats. That tariff sheet has not been revised in years, and 2026 listings for packaged Mandeh trips quote between roughly 650,000 and 1,500,000 rupiah depending on the route and whether lunch, gear and insurance are included. And if you are two people rather than twelve, the per boat rate is the whole point: either join a group leaving the same morning, or accept that the day costs what a day costs. Ask your homestay the night before, not on the jetty.
Before you fly: the airport, the train and your data

Minangkabau airport has its own rail link, the Minangkabau Express, which runs into Pulau Aie station in Padang's old town in about 45 minutes for a token fare, with roughly six departures a day. It is the cheapest and least stressful way in, but the timetable is thin, so check it against your arrival before you assume it. Otherwise an airport taxi does the same run in under an hour.
Sort a connection before you land. An
Indonesia eSIM from Airalo
means you have maps and messaging from the moment you clear the terminal, which matters more here than on Bali: on the bay side almost everything is arranged by WhatsApp, including the boats.
Day 1: Land at Padang and settle in the old town
Morning.
Arrive, activate your data, take the airport train or a taxi into town. Do not schedule anything else. Most useful arrivals into Padang connect through Jakarta and land tired.
Afternoon.

Walk the Kota Tua, the old town along the Batang Arau river, which is a run of Dutch and Chinese trading houses in various states of repair, then cross the bridge and climb Gunung Padang for the view back over the river mouth. It takes an hour and it orients you.
Evening.

Eat properly. Padang food is the reason half the country knows this city, and the local version bears little resemblance to the nasi Padang sold elsewhere in Indonesia. Sate Padang, with its thick yellow sauce, is the thing to have on the first night.
Base:
Two nights in Padang. Book
rooms in Padang
near the old town or Padang Beach rather than out by the airport.
Travel note:
Padang Beach itself is a city beach, good for sunset and street food, not for swimming.
Day 2: The Bungus islands, a warm-up day on the water
Morning.

Drive or ride south to Bungus, about forty minutes, or on to Sungai Pisang a little further. Boats leave from both for the near islands: Pasumpahan, Pagang, Sirandah and Sikuai. From Sungai Pisang a return boat to Pasumpahan has been quoted at around 35,000 to 50,000 rupiah per person; organised open trips out of Bungus run closer to 230,000 to 250,000 per person including the boat, entry, lunch and snorkel gear.
Afternoon.

Snorkel, swim, lie about. Pasumpahan is the easy pick: a short crossing, a sand spit and reef close enough to shore that you do not need a guide. Take your own mask if you are particular, because the rental gear is tired.
Evening.
Back to Padang for a second dinner in town. This is your last night with real restaurant choice for four days, so use it.
Booking logic:
Nothing needs booking in advance here. Turn up at the jetty, agree a price and a pickup time, and pay on return.
Travel note:
These islands are busy at weekends with local day trippers and near empty midweek. If your dates allow, do this on a weekday.
Day 3: South to Mandeh, and the viewpoint everyone comes for
Morning.

Leave Padang after breakfast. The drive south to Carocok Tarusan is roughly 55 to 60 kilometres and takes about ninety minutes, sometimes two hours if the coast road is busy. It is a good drive, coastal for much of it.
Afternoon.

Stop at Puncak Mandeh, the ridge viewpoint above the bay. This is the photograph the whole region is marketed on, and it earns it: the islands, the headlands and the mangrove fringe all in one frame. Entry is a token amount, quoted between 5,000 and 10,000 rupiah in recent listings and free at some access points. Go late afternoon rather than midday.
Evening.
Check in on the bay and eat where you sleep. There is no restaurant scene here, and that is fine; homestay food on this coast is generally better than the alternative.
Base:
Three nights around Mandeh village or Sungai Nyalo. Compare
stays around Mandeh and the bay
, and message the property directly about boats before you arrive.
Booking logic:
Arrange tomorrow's boat tonight. Ask your host to find you seats on a boat that is already going out, which is how two people avoid paying twelve people's worth of charter.
Day 4: The full island loop in Carocok Tarusan Bay
Morning.

Out early, before the wind gets up. The standard full loop takes in Sironjong Gadang, which has the best snorkelling in the bay and a decent beach, and Sironjong Ketek, which is where people jump off the cliff. That jump is commonly described as ten to twelve metres. It is not supervised in any meaningful way, and nobody will stop you doing something stupid.
Afternoon.

Continue past Cubadak, through the Sungai Gemuruh channel and on to Pulau Setan, the small island most day trips finish on. Setan has shade, a beach and basic camping if you ever want to come back and stay out here.
Evening.
Back to the mainland by late afternoon. Rinse the salt off, eat, sleep early.
Booking logic:
Agree the exact island list before you leave the jetty, not the price alone. Boatmen will happily shorten a loop if the sea turns, and you want that conversation to happen on land.
Travel note:
There is almost no shade on the boats. Long sleeves beat sunscreen here, both for you and for the reef.
Day 5: The mangroves, Kapo-Kapo and a slow day
Morning.

Take the mangrove half of the bay, which most day trips skip entirely. The Sungai Nyalo channels are quiet, shallow and best done by kayak or a small boat with the engine off. This is the part of Mandeh that is actually unlike anywhere else in West Sumatra.
Afternoon.

Stop at Kapo-Kapo, a small fishing village built out over the water on stilts, reachable only by boat. Go with someone local, buy something, and remember that people live there and are not part of the itinerary.
Evening.
Nothing scheduled. This is the day the trip earns its three nights.
Booking logic:
If the previous day was cut short by weather, this is your spare. Repeat the island loop instead and move the mangroves to the morning of Day 6.
Day 6: Painan, then back north along the coast
Morning.

Move thirty minutes south to Painan, the district town, and Carocok Painan, its beach. There is a causeway out to a small island, a fort hill above the bay and, unusually for this coast, somewhere to buy things.
Afternoon.
Either stay the night in Painan for a change of scene, or drive back north to Padang and give yourself a clean airport morning. Both work; the second is safer if your flight is early.
Base:
One night in
Painan
or back in
Padang
, depending on your flight time.
Travel note:
The coast road between Painan and Padang is the same road both ways and it is slow after dark. Leave in daylight.
Day 7: Padang food, and the flight out
Morning.

If you are in Padang, spend it eating. A proper Padang restaurant serves by hidangan, a dozen small dishes landing on the table at once, and you pay only for what you touch. Rendang is the famous one; the fish and the gulai are usually the better order.
Afternoon.
Take the Minangkabau Express or a taxi to the airport. Allow more time than the distance suggests, because the road north out of Padang backs up.
Travel note:
If you have a spare day, this is the moment to extend north rather than fly home. The
Bukittinggi and Harau Valley route
starts from the same airport.
What to book early, and what to keep flexible
Book early:
flights into Padang, especially around Indonesian public holidays, and your first two nights in the city. That is genuinely it.
Book a few days out:
the bay side rooms, because there are not many of them and the good ones are small. Message directly rather than relying on listings.
Keep flexible:
every boat. Weather decides this trip. Do not prepay a multi-day boat package from abroad, because you are buying away the only flexibility you have.
Mistakes travellers make on this coast
Coming as a day trip from Padang.
Three hours of driving for four hours in the bay, arriving in the middle of the day when the light is flat and the wind is up. It is the most common version of this trip and the worst one.
Booking a stay on Cubadak.
The resort closed in 2021. If a listing offers you a room there, it is stale.
Expecting a dive trip.
There is no established dive operation on the bay. If diving is the point of your Sumatra trip, go to
Pulau Weh
instead and treat Mandeh as a snorkelling week.
Turning up at the jetty to charter.
You will pay the whole boat. Arrange it the night before through your homestay and join a boat that is already going.
Travelling in November.
It is reliably the wettest month on this coast, and a wet week here means no boats at all, not just damp ones.
What to cut, adapt or upgrade
Cut it to five days
by dropping the Bungus day and going straight south on arrival. You lose the warm-up and the weather buffer, and you keep the bay itself.
Adapt it for families
by basing in Painan rather than on the bay, where the rooms are more conventional, and taking two half-day boats instead of one full day.
Upgrade it to twelve days

by adding the highlands: Padang, the Mandeh coast, then north to Bukittinggi, Lake Maninjau and the Harau Valley. That is the version we would actually book, and it is the strongest week and a half in West Sumatra.
Extend it much further
by treating this as the coastal opening of a longer Sumatra route. See the
15-day Sumatra itinerary
for how the north of the island connects.
How does Mandeh compare with Sumatra's other coasts?

Mandeh is the easiest coastal week in Sumatra to reach and the least equipped when you get there. Pulau Weh is the opposite: harder to reach, but it has an actual dive industry and rooms built for travellers. The Mentawai Islands are the remote option, and cost accordingly.

cells: Mandeh Bay, West Sumatra
Sheltered snorkelling, mangroves, short boat hops, ninety minutes from an airport
No dive industry, very simple rooms, boats priced by the boat
Pulau Weh, Aceh
Real diving, dive centres, an island you can settle into for a week
Two flights or a long overland haul from most of Sumatra
The Mentawai Islands
Surf, rainforest and a genuinely remote feel
Slow weather-dependent ferries and the highest costs of the three

children.text: Before you build this trip
Cash.
There are ATMs in Padang and Painan and effectively none on the bay. Boats, homestays and food are cash. Draw more than you think in Painan on the way south.
Language.
English drops off sharply outside Padang. A translation app that works offline is worth more here than on any Bali trip.
Sea conditions.
The bay is sheltered, which is why boats run when the open coast is closed, but the crossing out to the further islands is not. Believe your boatman.
Alcohol.
West Sumatra is conservative and largely dry outside a handful of hotels in Padang. Do not plan evenings around it.
Prices.
Every rupiah figure here is a working estimate drawn from published tariffs and recent operator listings, and this is a market where rates move without notice. Confirm on the day.
Final verdict

Mandeh is worth a week, and it is worth it for narrow reasons. If you want a coast where you can spend three days on small boats without ever queueing, where the mangroves are empty and the nearest thing to a tourist scene is a viewpoint with a parking attendant, this is one of the few places in Indonesia that still delivers that within two hours of an international airport.

If you want the version the marketing promises, the Raja Ampat comparison and an island resort to come back to at night, it is not here any more and has not been since 2021. Go knowing that, and West Sumatra's coast is the most underrated week we have written up in Sumatra. Go expecting a resort, and you will spend the week mildly disappointed by somewhere very good.

faq.answer: Three nights on the bay is the sweet spot, inside a week that starts and ends in Padang. One full day covers the island loop, a second covers the mangroves and Kapo-Kapo, and the third absorbs the weather day you will probably lose. Day trips from Padang technically work but waste most of the drive.
faq.question: How many days do you need in Mandeh Bay?

faq.answer: No. Cubadak Paradiso Village, the island's only resort, closed permanently on 31 August 2021 and nothing has replaced it. Older listings and aggregator pages still show it. Cubadak is now a stop on a boat loop, and you sleep on the mainland at Mandeh, Sungai Nyalo or Painan instead.
faq.question: Can you still stay on Pulau Cubadak?

faq.answer: By road, roughly 55 to 60 kilometres south of Padang to Carocok Tarusan, which takes about ninety minutes and sometimes two hours. Most people hire a car with a driver for the day or arrange a transfer through their homestay. There is no useful public transport link for the last stretch.
faq.question: How do you get from Padang to Mandeh?

faq.answer: Boats are chartered whole, not by the seat, and carry about twelve people. The published tariff for the Mandeh area lists a short island loop at around 750,000 rupiah and the fuller loop with the mangroves at around 850,000, while 2026 packaged trips are quoted between roughly 650,000 and 1,500,000.
faq.question: How much does a boat around Mandeh Bay cost?

faq.answer: It is good rather than exceptional. Sironjong Gadang has the clearest water and the most fish, the coral elsewhere is patchy, and visibility is best in the drier months from May to September. Compared with Pulau Weh or Raja Ampat it is modest, but you will often have a site to yourself.
faq.question: Is the snorkelling in Mandeh Bay any good?

faq.answer: Roughly May to September, with July often the driest month. November is reliably the wettest and the worst month for boats. Sumatra's west coast is wet year round, so treat any month as a probability rather than a promise and check a recent forecast before locking in boat days.
faq.question: When is the best time to visit the Mandeh coast?

faq.answer: It works with older children and is harder with toddlers. The days are boat days with little shade, the rooms on the bay are basic, and medical facilities are in Painan or Padang. Basing in Painan and taking two half-day boats instead of one long one makes it considerably easier.

heroImage.alt: Wooden boats moored over shallow reef below a forested headland in Mandeh Bay, West Sumatra

intro: West Sumatra's coast is the half of the province nobody plans for. Everyone lands at Padang and drives north to Bukittinggi. Ninety minutes south there is a sheltered bay of small islands and mangrove channels called Mandeh, and one large trap: the island resort that made it famous closed in 2021 and half the internet has not noticed.
